checklist.why: States the job: actions-page footer, Back left, category tabs right
No when-not (for example a sheet footer with Back + primary)
Back, tabs, active underline and handle named
One variant, used by both action pages
Tab pressed is "not drawn" and disabled dims; no rendered state set
No cap on the number of categories (the law says three strips)
Active tab: 700 weight + 3px underline, not colour only
One-word rule stated, but no overflow or under-310px example
aria-current=location, nav aria-label, focus rings stated
Raw px (86, 92, 14/18/28, 310) in CSS; no variable list
The 375 preview shows one state only; no overflow or narrow render

variants.name: default
findings: Screens show Production · Health · General; the README and the verb-sheet law say Health · Routine · Production

findings.text: Category names and order on screens (Production, Health, General) contradict the README and the verb-sheet law (Health, Routine, Production).
findings.fix: Pick one: rename General to Routine and order Health · Routine · Production in actionCatalogue, or change the law. The footer renders whatever order it is given.

findings.text: `disabled` dims a tab to half opacity, which the DS law forbids (nothing else is ever greyed).
findings.fix: Remove the disabled option from categoryFooter; callers leave out an empty category.

findings.text: The preview shows a single state: no scrolled or overflowing tabs, no under-310px shrink, no focus.
findings.fix: Add a 5-category instance at 300px width and a focused tab to preview.html.

findings.text: Raw px widths and paddings instead of back-width, control-height and footer tokens.
findings.fix: Swap 86px for back-width, 48px for control-height, and the padding for the footer tokens.

resolution.note: Findings addressed in the component pass; original judge scores preserved.
changes: Catalogue order Health, Routine, Production; General renamed Routine.
Disabled option removed from implementation and types.
Pressed, focus, empty, Chinese and five-category 300px states rendered; semantic footer tokens.
